sections.skill: Estimate closing costs and use mortgage disclosures to compare and verify loans

questions.prompt: Closing costs often run about 2% to 5% of the loan amount. For a $240,000 loan, what is the range?
questions.intro: Closing costs are fees paid to complete a home purchase: lender fees, appraisal, title insurance, recording fees, prepaid taxes and insurance, and more. They are in addition to the down payment.
questions.topic: Closing costs, the Loan Estimate, and the Closing Disclosure
sources: CFPB (Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure): Lenders must provide a Loan Estimate within 3 business days of a mortgage application and a Closing Disclosure at least 3 business days before closing. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/)

questions.prompt: The Lees apply for a mortgage on a Monday. The lender's offices are open Monday through Friday, and there are no holidays that week. By when must the lender deliver or mail their Loan Estimate?

choices.text: Only after the home is appraised

questions.intro: Federal rules require a standard three-page Loan Estimate within 3 business days of applying. It shows the rate, monthly payment, closing costs, and cash needed to close, making offers easy to compare.
questions.feedback: Within 3 business days after Monday (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday): by Thursday.
questions.topic: Closing costs, the Loan Estimate, and the Closing Disclosure
sources: CFPB (Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure): Lenders must provide a Loan Estimate within 3 business days of a mortgage application and a Closing Disclosure at least 3 business days before closing. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/)

questions.prompt: The Lees' closing is set for a Friday, with no holidays that week. By which day at the latest must they receive the Closing Disclosure? (For this rule, every day except Sundays and federal holidays counts as a business day.)
questions.intro: The Closing Disclosure lists the final loan terms and costs. Borrowers must receive it at least 3 business days before closing so they can compare it with the Loan Estimate.
questions.feedback: Counting back 3 business days from Friday: Thursday, Wednesday, Tuesday.
questions.topic: Closing costs, the Loan Estimate, and the Closing Disclosure

misconceptions.B: Too late to review before signing

questions.prompt: Cash to close: down payment $60,000 + closing costs $7,200 − $2,000 seller credit. How much cash do the Lees need at closing?
questions.intro: Cash to close = down payment + closing costs − credits (such as a seller credit or deposit already paid).

questions.prompt: The Closing Disclosure shows a rate of 6.9%, but the Loan Estimate showed 6.5% with the rate locked. What should the Lees do?

choices.text: Sign anyway, since small differences are normal and expected
Ignore it, since the Loan Estimate was only a guess
Ask the lender to explain or correct it before signing
Pay extra to speed up closing

questions.correct_answer: Ask the lender to explain or correct it before signing
questions.intro: Comparing the Closing Disclosure with the Loan Estimate catches changes or errors before you sign.
questions.feedback: A locked rate should not change; question any differences before closing.

questions.prompt: What does an appraisal do?

choices.text: Inspects the home only for needed repairs and safety issues
Guarantees the home will sell for that price later
Estimates the home's market value for the lender

questions.correct_answer: Estimates the home's market value for the lender
questions.intro: An appraisal estimates value; a home inspection checks condition. Lenders require appraisals to protect their collateral.
questions.feedback: Appraisals estimate value for the lender.

questions.prompt: An office is open Monday through Friday and closed weekends; there are no holidays in this period. Counting from a Monday, how many of its business days are there through the following Wednesday (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday)?
questions.intro: For an office open Monday through Friday, business days exclude weekends and holidays. (Mortgage rules use their own definitions: for the Closing Disclosure waiting period, Saturdays count as business days.)
questions.feedback: Seven weekdays from Tuesday to the next Wednesday.

questions.intro: Page 1 of the Loan Estimate shows the projected monthly payment, including principal and interest and estimated escrow for taxes and insurance.

questions.intro: Origination charges are the lender's own fees, which can be negotiated or compared across lenders.

questions.prompt: A Loan Estimate shows "Rate Lock: YES, until 4/15." What does that mean?

choices.text: The rate can never change for the full 30 years
The quoted rate is held until April 15, if the loan facts do not change
The rate changes daily until closing

questions.correct_answer: The quoted rate is held until April 15, if the loan facts do not change
questions.intro: A rate lock holds a quoted rate for a set period while the loan is processed. It depends on its terms: if the loan amount, the borrower's credit or income, or the property value changes, the rate can change.
questions.feedback: A lock holds the rate until its expiration date, as long as the loan and borrower facts stay the same.

questions.intro: The Loan Estimate includes comparison figures such as total paid in 5 years and APR.
questions.feedback: The 5-year total compares costs over a common period.

questions.prompt: Where does the Lees' cash to close usually need to come from?

choices.text: A personal check written that morning, in all cases
A cashier's check or verified wire, following verified instructions

questions.correct_answer: A cashier's check or verified wire, following verified instructions
questions.intro: Closings usually require certified funds or a wire. Wire fraud targeting homebuyers is common, so verify wiring instructions by phone using a known number.
questions.feedback: Certified funds or verified wires are standard; verify instructions independently.

Reply to the email to confirm
Split the wire between both accounts to be safe, just in case
Call the title company at a known phone number to verify

questions.intro: Changed wiring instructions are a major red flag for real estate wire fraud.

questions.prompt: What is title insurance?

choices.text: Protection against problems with who legally owns the property
Insurance that protects the lender if the buyer stops paying the loan
Insurance against defects found after moving in

questions.correct_answer: Protection against problems with who legally owns the property
questions.intro: Title insurance protects against problems with ownership records, such as unknown liens or errors in the deed.

questions.prompt: Which document gives the buyer legal ownership of the home?
questions.intro: Closing documents: the promissory note is the promise to repay; the mortgage pledges the home as collateral; title insurance protects against ownership problems; the deed transfers ownership and is recorded with the local government.

misconceptions.D: Protects ownership but does not transfer it
